subject: working with RRO open 3.21 and sharing a library with cran packages

messages.author: 5b1ca1066a6327d2
messages.subject: working with RRO open 3.21 and sharing a library with cran packages
parts:
Hi,
I understand that RRO open 3.2.1 can work side-by-side with standard CRAN R. To what extent does this extended compatibility hold? With standard R and Rstudio, I have a folder called RpersonalLib where I install all packages that I need over and above that provided by a standard R instalation.

The Rprofile.site for my CRAN R has the following addition :
.libPaths(c('C:/RpersonalLib','C:/R/R-3.2.1/library'))

To work in a similiar manner with RRO open 3.2.1, should I create a similiar folder called, let's say, RROownLib and install packages from MRAN there? Or, can I continue to use the RpersonalLib folder with CRAN packages in the .libPaths list? The question really boils down to the compatibility of RRO with CRAN packages. I can think of some cases where certain packages are dependent on MKL that comes along with RRO. There could be a difference between MRAN and CRAN packages in such a case. Or not?

Are the CRAN and MRAN packages interchangeable? In that case, how does a need for a seperate MRAN arise?
Or, are the CRAN and MRAN  two seperate silos with each intended for use only with their respective R installations?

I am looking forward to working with RRO.
Ravi

messages.author: 2aed7cbfca222ffd
messages.subject: Re: working with RRO open 3.21 and sharing a library with cran packages
parts:
Hello Ravi,

The easiest thing to do would be to edit the 'Rprofile.site' file that gets installed with RRO and add the following line to it:

options(repos = c(MYREPO = "https:/cran.fhcrc.org", CRAN = https://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/snapshot/2015-07-01)

For installing packages it will always use the first setting for 'repos', but you can have additional settings and change the current one on the fly in your current R session.


Hope this helps.

Stephen Weller
Revolution R Open Technical Support

messages.author: 2aed7cbfca222ffd
messages.subject: Re: working with RRO open 3.21 and sharing a library with cran packages
parts:
Yes, you can certainly change the value of .libPaths() and change it the same way you are currently doing with CRAN-R and it will use that as the destination folder in which to install your R add-on libraries. To make this change permanent, add it to the 'Rprofile.site' file under:

C:\Program Files\RRO\R-3.2.1\etc

For example, add the following to the bottom of this file:
.libPaths("C:\Users\testRuser\MyRLibrary")
